flashcard_questions.q: A popular Elizabethan and Jacobean entertainment where a bear was chained to a post and attacked by dogs, held in arenas near theatres like the Globe.
When the outcome of a situation is the opposite of what was expected, often used to highlight a character’s misunderstanding.
The moment in a Greek tragedy when the tragic hero recognises the truth about their situation, often too late to change the outcome.

flashcard_questions.a: A sudden reversal of fortune in a tragedy, often marking the beginning of the tragic hero’s downfall.
A fatal flaw in a tragic hero’s character that leads to their downfall — from Aristotle’s theory of tragedy.
